positions.commentary: The speaker uses McDonald's as a hypothetical example of how to evaluate a business, focusing on past performance, cash flows, and demographics rather than market speculation.
The speaker states that the subject understood Amazon really well and did not want to change his position because he understood the business was exceptional.
The speaker mentions that Nick Sleep's portfolio was heavily concentrated in Costco and Berkshire Hathaway alongside Amazon, with Costco making up a significant portion of the remaining capital.
The speaker recommends reading Nick Sleep's letters, which are available via a Google search, describing them as essential reading for investors.

thesis: This episode argues that investors should focus on understanding great businesses deeply and holding them for the long term, rather than engaging in market speculation. It highlights the value of studying specific investor letters, such as those from Nick Sleep, to learn how to identify and maintain positions in exceptional companies like Amazon and Costco.

claims.claim: The speaker uses McDonald's as a hypothetical example of how to evaluate a business, focusing on past performance, cash flows, and demographics rather than market speculation.
claims.quote: So if you were going to buy a McDonald's in Clemson and someone want to sell it, what you'd be focused on is how has that McDonald's performed in the last few years, what kind of cash flows it's produced, what are the demographics of Clemson looking like for the next few years?

claims.claim: The speaker cites Nick Sleep's 2014 position in Amazon, noting it was $300 a share at the time and is now worth over $3,300, illustrating the value of owning great businesses long-term.
claims.quote: At that time in 2014, Amazon was $300 a share. Now it's $3,300 or more than that. So what he did in with his partner, Zach, is he wrote to his investor saying, look, I'm returning on your capital, I'm shutting down my funds.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Nick Sleep's portfolio was heavily concentrated in Costco and Berkshire Hathaway alongside Amazon, with Costco making up a significant portion of the remaining capital.
claims.quote: And then Costco and Berksha Hathaway made up almost the rest of the portfolio. So 90% of the portfolio was Amazon Costco and Berksha happening. Okay? That's how he was running his portfolio.

claims.claim: The speaker recommends reading Nick Sleep's letters, which are available via a Google search, describing them as essential reading for investors.
claims.quote: So I think if you do a Google search, just Nick Sleep letters, it'll bring up some links which will give you all his letters. I think those are like the Dead Sea Scrolls. They should be required reading.

claims.claim: The speaker states that the subject understood Amazon really well and did not want to change his position because he understood the business was exceptional.
claims.quote: The UK regulators were giving him a lot of grief saying you cannot have all this risk in a portfolio with so much money in one position and that you need to diversify. And it went against every bone in his body because he understood Amazon really well. He did not want to change even 10 years from now his Amazon position because he understood that business was exceptional.
